# AI voice disclosure and automated call identification

> Informational, not legal advice. Laws change and courts interpret them; confirm with a lawyer licensed in the jurisdiction before relying on any rule here.

Data: [`data/call-desk/ai-disclosure.json`](../data/call-desk/ai-disclosure.json). Read on primary sources as of 2026-10-11.

## Federal

| Jurisdiction | Rule | What to disclose | When | Effective | Citation | As of |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United States (federal) | FCC Declaratory Ruling: AI-generated voices are "artificial" voices under the TCPA | No AI-specific disclosure. Because AI voices count as "artificial or prerecorded voice", outbound AI voice calls need the called party's prior express consent (prior express written consent for telemarketing under 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2)) and must follow the identification rules of 47 CFR 64.1200(b). | Consent before the call; identification at the start of the message. | 2024-02-08 | [FCC 24-17, CG Docket No. 23-362 (released 2024-02-08); 47 U.S.C. 227(b)](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-17A1.pdf) | 2026-10-11 |
| United States (federal) | Identification required in artificial or prerecorded voice messages | The legal name of the business responsible for the call, then a callback telephone number; for telemarketing, an automated way to opt out. | Identity at the beginning of the message; the number during or after it. |  | [47 CFR 64.1200(b)(1)-(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200) | 2026-10-11 |
| Canada (federal) | CRTC ADAD Rules: opening identification | Who the call is on behalf of and a brief description of its purpose, plus an email or postal address and a local or toll-free number; repeated at the end if the message runs past 60 seconds. ADAD means a prerecorded or synthesized voice. Telemarketing by ADAD also needs the consumer's prior express consent for that number (Part IV s.2). | At the beginning of the call. |  | [CRTC Unsolicited Telecommunications Rules, Part IV (ADAD Rules), s.4(d)](https://crtc.gc.ca/eng/trules-reglest.htm) | 2026-10-11 |

## AI disclosure by state

| Jurisdiction | Rule | What to disclose | When | Effective | Citation | As of |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Utah | Utah generative AI consumer disclosures | That the person is interacting with generative AI and not a human. Regulated occupations (licensed professions) must also disclose prominently, without being asked, in high-risk interactions involving health, financial or biometric data or medical, legal, financial or mental health advice. | When the person clearly asks whether AI is being used. For regulated occupations in high-risk interactions: verbally at the start of a voice interaction. Safe harbor (13-77-104): disclose at the outset and throughout. | 2025-05-07 | [Utah Code 13-77-103, 13-77-104 (S.B. 226, Laws 2025 ch. 465; replaced former 13-2-12)](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter77/C13-77-S103_2025050720250507.html) | 2026-10-11 |
| Utah | Utah mental health chatbots | That the chatbot is AI and not a human. | Before access, at the start of any interaction after 7 days without use, and whenever asked. | 2025-05-07 | [Utah Code 13-72a-203 (H.B. 452, Laws 2025 ch. 269)](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter72a/C13-72a-S203_2025050720250507.html) | 2026-10-11 |
| Maine | Maine transparency in consumer transactions involving AI | That the consumer is not engaging with a human being. Covers AI chatbots that communicate by text or voice. | Whenever the AI could mislead a reasonable consumer into believing it is human; clear and conspicuous, no fixed timing. | 2025-09-24 | [10 M.R.S. 1500-DD (P.L. 2025, c. 294, enacted as 1500-Y; reallocated by R.R. 2025, c. 1)](https://legislature.maine.gov/statutes/10/title10sec1500-DD-1.html) | 2026-10-11 |
| California | California artificial voice notice for automatic dialing-announcing devices (AB 2905) | Before the device plays anything, a live, unrecorded natural voice must state the nature of the call and the business name, address and phone, ask whether the person consents to hear the message, and say whether the message uses an artificial voice (one generated or significantly altered using AI). | At the start of the call, by a live person, before the recorded or AI message. | 2025-01-01 | [Cal. Pub. Util. Code 2874(a)(3), (c) (Stats. 2024, Ch. 316, AB 2905)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=2874) | 2026-10-11 |
| California | California generative AI in patient communications (AB 3030) | That the communication was generated by generative AI, and how the patient can reach a human health care provider. | For audio: spoken at the start and at the end of the interaction. | 2025-01-01 | [Cal. Health & Safety Code 1339.75 (Stats. 2024, Ch. 848, AB 3030)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240AB3030) | 2026-10-11 |
| California | California BOT Act | That it is a bot. ## Automated call identification by state

| Jurisdiction | Rule | What to disclose | When | Effective | Citation | As of |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Texas | Texas ADAD message identification | The nature of the call, who is making it, and the calling number. | Within the first 30 seconds of the recorded message. | 1997-09-01 | [Tex. Util. Code 55.127](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/UT/htm/UT.55.htm) | 2026-10-11 |
| New York | New York ADAD message identification | The nature of the call and the name of the person it is sent for; their address and phone at the end. | At the beginning of the call. |  | [N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law 399-p(3)(a)](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/399-P) | 2026-10-11 |
| Nevada | Nevada ADAD natural-voice introduction | The nature of the call, that a prerecorded message follows, and the business name, address and phone. | Before the prerecorded message, by a recorded or live natural voice. |  | [NRS 597.814(1)](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-597.html) | 2026-10-11 |
| Minnesota | Minnesota ADAD live operator disclosure | The business name, the purpose, the goods or services, and whether payment is solicited. | At the outset, by a live operator before the message (the alternative to prior consent under 325E.27). |  | [Minn. Stat. 325E.29](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325E.29) | 2026-10-11 |
| North Dakota | North Dakota caller identification | The caller's true first and last name, telephone number, city and state, and the business name. | Immediately at the beginning of the call. |  | [N.D.C.C. 51-28-03, 51-28-07](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t51c28.pdf) | 2026-10-11 |
| Indiana | Indiana ADAD live operator disclosure | The business name, the purpose, the goods or services, and whether funds are solicited. | At the outset, by a live operator before the message. |  | [Ind. Code 24-5-14-7](https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_24/Article_5.pdf) | 2026-10-11 |
| Virginia | Virginia ADAD live operator disclosure | The entity sending the message, its purpose, the goods or services, and payment terms. | By a live operator immediately before the message. |  | [Va. Code 59.1-518.2; 59.1-512](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title59.1/chapter44.1/section59.1-518.2/) | 2026-10-11 |
| Washington | Washington telephone solicitor identification | The caller, the company or organization, and the purpose of the call. | Within the first 30 seconds. |  | [RCW 80.36.390(3); RCW 80.36.400](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=80.36.390) | 2026-10-11 |
| Michigan | Michigan telephone solicitor identification | The caller's name and the organization's full name. | At the beginning of the telephone solicitation. |  | [MCL 445.111b(1)](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-445-111b) | 2026-10-11 |
| Utah | Utah telephone solicitor identification | The telephone solicitor, the business it calls for, and the purpose of the call. | Promptly on making contact. |  | [Utah Code 13-25a-103(5)](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter25A/C13-25a-S103_2022050420220504.html) | 2026-10-11 |
| Florida | Florida telephone solicitor identification | The solicitor's true first and last name and the business it calls for. | Immediately on making contact. |  | [Fla. Stat. 501.059(2)](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/501.059) | 2026-10-11 |
| Oregon | Oregon ADAD opt-out | A way to opt out with a single keypress, described in the prerecorded or synthesized message; no misrepresenting identity or purpose. | Usable within the first 10 seconds of the call. | 2026-01-01 | [ORS 646A.372(1)(a)(B); 646A.374(2), as amended by Or.
